name: Tawantinsuyu ("Inca Empire")
notes: The empire’s self-designation, "the four regions/parts together" (Chinchaysuyu, Antisuyu, Collasuyu, Contisuyu radiating from Cusco); "Inca Empire" is a widely-used alias that conflates the ruler/ruling-elite term with the multiethnic state. The 1438 founding date (Pachacuti Inca Yupanqui’s ascension, per John Rowe’s classical 1945/46 chronology built from colonial king-lists) is the traditional figure but has been directly challenged by more recent Bayesian-refined radiocarbon dating (Cambridge University Press/Radiocarbon journal), with at least one peer-reviewed source concluding "1438 should not be used as a starting date for the Inca polity and history" — see claim_pachacuti_dating_revision. Organized political resistance continued 40 years past the 1532 Cajamarca capture of Atahualpa, via the Neo-Inca State at Vilcabamba (founded 1537 by Manco Inca Yupanqui), until Vilcabamba’s fall and Túpac Amaru’s execution in 1572 — the entity’s date_range latest reflects this 1572 end of organized resistance, not the 1532 capture, which is a documented popular-narrative omission (see claim_tawantinsuyu_fall_multicausal).
